uncited: It builds on [Object Decomposition and Composition](14518-object-decomposition-and-composition.md) by using a learnable object code conditioned on spatial position rather than fixed segmentation masks.
**NeRF Backbone:** Learns volume density and appearance.
**Object Field:** Learns a unique object code for every 3D point.
The network takes positional encoding $\text{PE}(x,y,z)$ for location and $\text{PE}(\theta,\phi)$ for viewing direction as input.
*   Object Code $\mathbf{o} \in \mathbb{R}^{H+1}$: Function of location only.
**Forward Pass:** For each ray, sample points.
**Inverse Query:** Use a lightweight inverse query algorithm to edit the scene geometry.

*   Standard NeRF rendering loss (color difference) [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the method leverages a 'vanilla NeRF as the backbone' which 'predicts the volume density σ and color c'. Standard NeRF training relies on minimizing the difference between predicted and ground truth colors (color difference loss) to learn the radiance field. Since the DM-NeRF pipeline uses this standard NeRF backbone to learn appearance (color) and density, it inherently utilizes the standard NeRF rendering loss (color difference) as part of its optimization process, even if additional losses (for object codes) are added. Therefore, the claim that standard NeRF rendering loss is used is supported by the description of the backbone.
